body: satellites operating over the Arctic are plagued by a unique electromagnetic phenomenon
that occurs in the northern tier
. Ionospheric scintillation, the flickering and distortion of radio waves, is more prominent at the poles. While
does not damage satellites, it does
interfere with the transmission and reception of their signals

, which include signals received from position, navigation, and timing satellites such as the Global Positioning System.71 In addition, the Earth’s magnetic poles trap charged particles that can create electro-magnetic anomalies that hamper space-based sensor collection operations.72
